_comment: #892 Phase 3 — every CI step that ANNOUNCES it will never fail carries an owner, an issue and a date by which somebody decides whether it should stay advisory. scripts/ci/advisory-expiry.mjs fails on a missing entry, a missing field, a past `revisitBy`, or an entry naming a step that no longer exists. This is the same discipline the quarantine ledger, tests/env-red.json and every tighten-only budget already apply; a non-blocking annotation had none, and it is the place a real regression hides longest precisely because its normal state is 'there is output'.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: Report generat.why: A byte-exact rebuild of the browser Iroh binding is not hermetic across rustc/wasm-bindgen intrinsic comment renumbering, so drift cannot be a hard gate until the rebuild is reproducible. Rebuild SUCCESS is already the required half. The decision this date forces: either the rebuild has become reproducible (make drift blocking) or it has not (say so, and extend deliberately).

.github/workflows/ci.yml: Advisory — Exp.why: `expo ci:versions` prints a long pin-skew list; making it blocking today would drown real L4 failures under known, deliberate divergences. #646 tracks the hard Expo pin alignment that would let this fail closed. Until then it is a step that prints and exits 0 on every mobile PR, which is why it needs a date rather than a rationale alone.
